quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Filling the Gap] The consulting firm loses two major clients within the same quarter that its senior partner announces her retirement, and the remaining partners begin meeting weekly with a recruiter who specializes in client relations.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the reason for the partners' meetings with the recruiter?
options: The recruiter is unrelated to the client losses.
They may be trying to replace the expertise the retiring partner brought to client relationships.
They plan to close the firm entirely.
They are hiring someone to replace the lost clients as customers.
quests.correctAnswer: They may be trying to replace the expertise the retiring partner brought to client relationships.
quests.hint: Connect the timing of the retirement, the lost clients, and the type of recruiter they're now meeting.
quests.explanation: Losing clients around the same time a client-relations partner leaves, followed by meeting a client-relations recruiter, suggests the firm is trying to fill that specific gap in expertise.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Rotation Changes] Despite booking a direct flight, Renata's itinerary now lists a two-hour layover in a different city, and the airline's email mentions 'aircraft rotation changes' affecting several routes this month.
quests.question: What is the most likely reason for the change to Renata's itinerary?
options: The direct flight route was never available.
Renata personally requested the layover.
The airline adjusted its overall flight schedule, affecting multiple routes.
The change only affects Renata's specific booking.
quests.correctAnswer: The airline adjusted its overall flight schedule, affecting multiple routes.
quests.hint: Notice that the airline mentions this affects 'several routes,' not just one traveler.
quests.explanation: Mentioning changes affecting several routes suggests a broader scheduling adjustment, not something specific to Renata's booking alone.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [No More Daily Calls] After switching to the new inventory software, the warehouse manager stops receiving the daily phone calls from staff asking where specific items are stored.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the new inventory software?
options: It removed the need for a warehouse entirely.
It has made locating items more difficult.
It has made it easier for staff to locate items themselves.
It caused staff to stop working.
quests.correctAnswer: It has made it easier for staff to locate items themselves.
quests.hint: Think about what the disappearance of a recurring problem, right after the software switch, suggests.
quests.explanation: The daily location questions stopping right after the software switch suggests staff can now find items more easily on their own.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Non-Negotiable Stretch] The physical therapist reviews Mr. Coleman's exercise log, notices he skipped the stretching routine on the days he reported the most knee pain, and adjusts the plan to make stretching non-negotiable.
quests.question: What does the physical therapist likely believe about the missed stretching?
options: It is the cause of his overall recovery.
It has no relationship to his knee pain at all.
It should be removed from his plan completely.
It may be connected to his increased knee pain on those days.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be connected to his increased knee pain on those days.
quests.hint: Notice which days the pain was worse and what he had skipped on those same days.
quests.explanation: Making stretching mandatory right after noticing it was missing on high-pain days suggests the therapist believes the two are connected.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Lisbon Bakery] Every time the extended family gathers, someone brings up the trip to Lisbon a decade ago, and the conversation always circles back to the afternoon they got lost looking for a specific bakery.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the Lisbon trip?
options: It happened only last month.
It was a trip nobody enjoyed at all.
Only one family member remembers the trip.
It holds a special, shared significance for the family.
quests.correctAnswer: It holds a special, shared significance for the family.
quests.hint: Think about what returning to the same memory, every single time they gather, suggests about its importance.
quests.explanation: Repeatedly returning to the same memory at every gathering suggests the Lisbon trip holds lasting, shared meaning for the family.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Well-Timed Coupon] The store's loyalty app sends Fatima a coupon for dog food the same week she buys a leash and a small dog bed for the first time.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how the loyalty app selects its coupons?
options: It tailors offers based on a customer's recent purchases.
It sends the same coupons to every customer.
It has no connection to purchase history.
It only sends coupons randomly once a year.
quests.correctAnswer: It tailors offers based on a customer's recent purchases.
quests.hint: Think about the connection between her recent purchases and the coupon she received.
quests.explanation: Sending a dog food coupon right after she buys a leash and dog bed suggests the app tailors offers to recent purchases.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Persistent Waitlist] The university adds extra sections of the introductory statistics course each of the last three semesters, yet the waitlist still has over forty names within a day of registration opening.
quests.question: What can be inferred about student demand for the course?
options: It continues to exceed the available spots despite expansion.
It has been fully met by the added sections.
It is decreasing every semester.
No students are interested in taking it.
quests.correctAnswer: It continues to exceed the available spots despite expansion.
quests.hint: Think about whether the waitlist shrank or stayed large even after more sections were added.
quests.explanation: A waitlist of forty names, even after three semesters of added sections, suggests demand keeps outpacing the available spots.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Third Season] The streaming platform renews the low-budget drama for a third season despite modest viewership, while cancelling two flashier shows that initially drew larger audiences but saw sharp drops by episode three.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the low-budget drama's audience?
options: It lost viewers faster than the other two shows.
It has likely kept a steady, loyal viewership over time.
It was cancelled due to low interest.
It had the largest audience of the three shows.
quests.correctAnswer: It has likely kept a steady, loyal viewership over time.
quests.hint: Compare how the drama's numbers likely held up against the sharp drops described for the other two shows.
quests.explanation: Being renewed despite modest numbers, while shows with sharp viewer drops were cancelled, suggests the drama kept a steady audience rather than losing viewers quickly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Divided Committee Agrees] The city council approves funding for a new bike lane after a petition gathers signatures from residents on both sides of the usually divided traffic committee.
quests.question: What can be inferred about support for the bike lane?
options: It drew backing from people who do not typically agree.
It only had support from one side of the committee.
The petition failed to gather enough interest.
It was opposed by everyone on the committee.
quests.correctAnswer: It drew backing from people who do not typically agree.
quests.hint: Think about what it means for a 'usually divided' group to sign the same petition.
quests.explanation: Gathering signatures from both sides of a normally divided committee suggests the bike lane earned unusually broad support.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Creative but Inconsistent] The food critic gives the new fusion restaurant three stars for creativity but only one star for consistency, noting that the same dish tasted noticeably different on each of her two visits.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the restaurant's main challenge?
options: It lacks any creative or original ideas.
It only opened for a single day.
It struggles to prepare its dishes the same way each time.
It received the same rating for every category.
quests.correctAnswer: It struggles to prepare its dishes the same way each time.
quests.hint: Notice which score was low and what specific detail from her visits explains it.
quests.explanation: A low consistency score paired with the same dish tasting different on two visits suggests the restaurant struggles to replicate its dishes reliably.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Thin Air] Two of the four hikers turn back at the halfway marker, citing the thin air, while the other two continue on and mention feeling completely fine at that altitude.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the two hikers who continued?
options: They may be more acclimated to high altitudes than the other two.
They also experienced serious difficulty breathing.
They were unaware of the altitude at all.
They turned back before reaching the halfway point.
quests.correctAnswer: They may be more acclimated to high altitudes than the other two.
quests.hint: Compare how each pair described feeling at the same altitude.
quests.explanation: Feeling fine at an altitude that caused two others to turn back suggests those two hikers are more used to high elevations.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Rerouted Again] The navigation app reroutes drivers away from the highway exit for the third day in a row, always suggesting the same side street instead.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the highway exit?
options: It is the fastest route every day.
It is likely experiencing ongoing traffic problems or construction.
The app is malfunctioning randomly.
It has been permanently closed to all traffic.
quests.correctAnswer: It is likely experiencing ongoing traffic problems or construction.
quests.hint: Think about what causes a navigation app to consistently avoid the same route for several days.
quests.explanation: Rerouting away from the same exit for three days in a row suggests an ongoing issue there, such as traffic or construction.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Bending the Policy] Two employees request the same Friday off, and though company policy allows only one absence per department that day, the manager approves both requests and quietly reassigns their tasks to the following Monday.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the manager's decision?
options: She fired one of the employees over the conflict.
She decided flexibility mattered more than strictly following the policy that day.
She denied both requests in the end.
She was completely unaware of the department's policy.
quests.correctAnswer: She decided flexibility mattered more than strictly following the policy that day.
quests.hint: Think about what approving both requests, despite the policy, and rearranging tasks afterward reveals about her priorities.
quests.explanation: Approving both requests despite the policy, then rearranging the workload, suggests the manager chose to prioritize flexibility over strict rule-following in this case.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Shorter Follow-Up] After the specialist reviews the scan and asks Mrs. Bello to schedule a follow-up in only two weeks instead of the usual six months, she also recommends bringing a family member to the next appointment.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the specialist's concern level?
options: She wants to reduce the frequency of visits.
She is cancelling all future appointments.
She wants to monitor the situation more closely than usual.
She believes everything is completely normal.
quests.correctAnswer: She wants to monitor the situation more closely than usual.
quests.hint: Compare the shortened follow-up window and the added suggestion with what would happen in a routine, unremarkable case.
quests.explanation: A much shorter follow-up window and a suggestion to bring family both point to the specialist wanting closer monitoring than a routine case would need.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Requested by Name] Every visit to her in-laws, Noor brings a dish from her own culture, and over the years, her mother-in-law has started requesting it by name before Noor even offers.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the mother-in-law's feelings toward the dish?
options: She only eats it to be polite once a year.
She has always disliked the dish.
She has never actually tasted it.
She has come to genuinely enjoy it.
quests.correctAnswer: She has come to genuinely enjoy it.
quests.hint: Think about what asking for something by name, unprompted, suggests about someone's true feelings toward it.
quests.explanation: Requesting the dish by name before being offered suggests the mother-in-law has grown to genuinely enjoy it over the years.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Tucked in a Back Corner] The bookstore's staff-picks shelf sells out three times faster than the bestseller display, even though the staff-picks section is tucked into a back corner with no special signage.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the staff-picks recommendations?
options: The bestseller display sells out faster than staff picks.
Customers trust them enough to seek them out despite their poor placement.
The staff-picks shelf is located in the most visible spot in the store.
Customers never notice the staff-picks shelf.
quests.correctAnswer: Customers trust them enough to seek them out despite their poor placement.
quests.hint: Think about what selling out quickly, despite an unfavorable location, suggests about customer trust in the recommendations.
quests.explanation: Selling out quickly despite a poor location suggests customers actively seek out and trust the staff-picks recommendations.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Scathing Review] The documentary's ticket sales spike sharply in the week after a well-known critic's scathing review goes viral online, surprising the small studio that produced it.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the effect of the negative review?
options: It had no impact on the film's visibility.
It convinced the studio to cancel the film's release.
It caused ticket sales to drop sharply.
It may have drawn more curiosity and attention to the film.
quests.correctAnswer: It may have drawn more curiosity and attention to the film.
quests.hint: Think about what a spike in ticket sales, right after a viral negative review, suggests about public curiosity.
quests.explanation: Ticket sales spiking right after a scathing review went viral suggests the controversy drew extra attention and curiosity to the film.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Second Dessert Table] The community potluck's sign-up sheet fills every open slot within a day, prompting the organizers to add a second table exclusively for desserts.
quests.question: What can be inferred about interest in this year's potluck?
options: No one signed up to bring dessert.
It is lower than in previous years.
The potluck was cancelled due to low interest.
It is higher than the original number of slots could accommodate.
quests.correctAnswer: It is higher than the original number of slots could accommodate.
quests.hint: Think about what quickly filling every slot, followed by adding an entirely new table, suggests about interest.
quests.explanation: Filling every slot within a day and needing an extra dessert table suggests interest in the potluck exceeded what organizers originally planned for.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Extra Medical Staff] The cruise line adds extra staff to the medical bay and stocks additional motion-sickness medication before departing on this particular route, more than it typically carries.
quests.question: What can be inferred about this route?
options: It is known for unusually calm waters.
It is likely known for rougher waters than other routes.
It requires no special preparation at all.
It is a route the cruise line has never sailed before.
quests.correctAnswer: It is likely known for rougher waters than other routes.
quests.hint: Think about what extra medical staff and motion-sickness medication, specifically for this route, suggests about conditions at sea.
quests.explanation: Stocking extra motion-sickness medication and staff specifically for this route suggests it tends to involve rougher waters than usual.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Irregular Readings] The wearable device alerts Mr. Tanaka to an irregular heartbeat pattern twice within a month, and both times, he had just finished back-to-back meetings without a lunch break.
quests.question: What might the pattern in the alerts suggest?
options: Skipping meals and back-to-back stress may be linked to the irregular readings.
Eating lunch always triggers the irregular readings.
The device only activates once a year.
The alerts occur completely at random with no pattern.
quests.correctAnswer: Skipping meals and back-to-back stress may be linked to the irregular readings.
quests.hint: Notice what both alert incidents had in common in terms of his schedule that day.
quests.explanation: Both alerts following meetings without a lunch break suggests a possible connection between skipped meals, stress, and the irregular readings.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Switching to a Human Interpreter] The translation earbuds handle Mateusz's casual conversations at the market smoothly, but during the business negotiation, he switches back to a human interpreter for the contract details.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Mateusz's confidence in the earbuds?
options: He has never used the earbuds successfully.
He trusts the earbuds completely, even for contracts.
He refuses to use the earbuds under any circumstances.
He trusts them more for simple exchanges than for high-stakes situations.
quests.correctAnswer: He trusts them more for simple exchanges than for high-stakes situations.
quests.hint: Compare the two different situations and which tool he chose for each.
quests.explanation: Using the earbuds casually but switching to a human interpreter for the contract suggests Mateusz trusts the technology more for low-stakes situations than critical ones.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [It Felt Right] The twins split the inheritance exactly down the middle, but one sibling quietly transfers a portion of their share back to the other a month later, mentioning only that 'it felt right.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the sibling who transferred the money back?
options: They wanted to end their relationship with their sibling.
They regretted receiving any inheritance at all.
They were required by law to give the money back.
They believed the original split was not entirely fair to the other sibling.
quests.correctAnswer: They believed the original split was not entirely fair to the other sibling.
quests.hint: Think about what voluntarily giving money back, even after an equal split, suggests about their sense of fairness.
quests.explanation: Giving part of an equal share back, saying it 'felt right,' suggests the sibling felt the original split did not fully account for something fair to the other person.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Coming In Anyway] The company offers every employee the option to work from home two days a week, but by the end of the first month, nearly all of the senior staff are still coming in five days a week regardless.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the senior staff's preference?
options: Most of them prefer working in the office despite having the option not to.
They were not allowed to use the new policy.
The company cancelled the new policy immediately.
They all switched to working from home entirely.
quests.correctAnswer: Most of them prefer working in the office despite having the option not to.
quests.hint: Think about what choosing not to use an available option, when everyone else could, suggests about personal preference.
quests.explanation: Continuing to come in five days despite having the option for remote work suggests most senior staff genuinely prefer working in the office.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Leftover Screws] The furniture store's delivery team reassembles the bookshelf on-site after noticing several screws were left over from the customer's earlier attempt to build it alone.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the customer's first attempt at assembly?
options: It likely did not go entirely as intended.
It was finished well ahead of schedule.
It was completed perfectly with no issues.
It required no tools or effort at all.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely did not go entirely as intended.
quests.hint: Think about what leftover screws usually indicate about how an assembly went.
quests.explanation: Leftover screws from the earlier attempt suggest the customer's first try at assembling the bookshelf did not go quite right.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Before Final Exams] The school nurse's office sees a noticeable rise in visits every year during the two weeks before final exams, mostly for headaches and stomachaches.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the cause of these visits?
options: They are caused by a seasonal illness every year.
They have no connection to the timing of exams.
They only happen during summer vacation.
They may be linked to exam-related stress among students.
quests.correctAnswer: They may be linked to exam-related stress among students.
quests.hint: Think about what happening at the same time every year, right before exams, suggests about the cause.
quests.explanation: A rise in headaches and stomachaches specifically before exams, every year, suggests these visits may be connected to stress about the tests.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Three More Languages] After the clinic starts offering appointments in three additional languages, the number of patients completing their full treatment plans rises noticeably over the next year.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the earlier language barrier?
options: It only affected the clinic's opening hours.
It had no effect on whether patients finished treatment.
It caused patients to complete treatment faster before.
It may have previously prevented some patients from completing treatment.
quests.correctAnswer: It may have previously prevented some patients from completing treatment.
quests.hint: Think about what improving after adding languages suggests about what was holding some patients back before.
quests.explanation: Treatment completion rising after adding more languages suggests the earlier language barrier may have been preventing some patients from finishing their care.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Free Recycling] The town's recycling participation more than doubles in the months after the city switches from a paid pickup service to a free one included in property taxes.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the previous paid pickup system?
options: It resulted in more recycling than the free system.
The cost may have discouraged some residents from recycling regularly.
It had no effect on how many residents recycled.
It was more popular than the new free service.
quests.correctAnswer: The cost may have discouraged some residents from recycling regularly.
quests.hint: Think about what participation doubling, right after the cost was removed, suggests about the earlier system.
quests.explanation: Recycling rates more than doubling after the service became free suggests the earlier cost had been discouraging some residents from participating.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A More Transparent Delay] The game studio delays the release date for the third time, but this time includes a lengthy developer video explaining specific bugs still being fixed, unlike the vague statements before.
quests.question: What can be inferred about this delay compared to the earlier ones?
options: This is the first delay the game has ever had.
The studio is hiding even more information than before.
The studio is being more transparent about the reasons this time.
The game has now been cancelled entirely.
quests.correctAnswer: The studio is being more transparent about the reasons this time.
quests.hint: Compare the level of detail given in this explanation with the earlier, vaguer statements.
quests.explanation: Providing a detailed explanation of specific bugs, unlike the vague statements before, suggests the studio is choosing to be more transparent this time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Wireless Syncing] The e-reader's battery lasts three weeks under normal use, but drops to under a week when Farah keeps the wireless syncing feature turned on at all times.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the wireless syncing feature?
options: It consumes a significant amount of battery power when left on.
It has no effect on battery life at all.
It extends the battery life significantly.
It only works when the battery is full.
quests.correctAnswer: It consumes a significant amount of battery power when left on.
quests.hint: Compare the battery life with the feature on versus off.
quests.explanation: The battery life dropping sharply when syncing stays on suggests this feature uses a significant amount of power.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Double the Points] The airline's frequent-flyer forum fills with complaints after the redesigned rewards program requires nearly double the points for the same flights members used to book.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the new rewards program?
options: It offers significantly more value than before.
It offers less value to members than the previous version.
It requires fewer points than the old program.
It was praised by every member on the forum.
quests.correctAnswer: It offers less value to members than the previous version.
quests.hint: Think about what needing almost double the points for the same flights suggests about the program's value.
quests.explanation: Requiring nearly double the points for the same flights suggests the redesigned program gives members less value than the previous one.
